records.authors: Lauranne Gateau-Rey; Edmund V. J. Tanner; Bruno Rapidel; Jean-Philippe Marelli; Stefan Royaert
records.external_validity_limits: Single Brazilian municipality near cocoa climatic limits; no untreated contemporaneous control; do not transfer the magnitude to West Africa
records.lag: Loss persisted into the following harvest
records.mechanism_use: Supports severe-drought tail-risk mechanism but not a West Africa effect size
records.reported_result: Potential main-harvest yield fell 89% and productive-tree mortality was 15%; the authors stress the event and location were exceptional
records.sample_or_data: 31 randomly selected farms with permanent transects
records.title: Climate change could threaten cocoa production: Effects of 2015-16 El Nino-related drought on cocoa agroforests in Bahia Brazil

records.authors: Bismark Kwesi Asitoakor; Richard Asare; Anders Raebild; Hans Peter Ravn; Vincent Yao Eziah; Kwadwo Owusu; Eric Opoku Mensah; Philippe Vaast
records.exposure: Rainfall temperature humidity shade and management across three zones
records.external_validity_limits: Only three communities and 23 farms; climate and management vary together; association is not a causal tonne response
records.mechanism_use: Supports dual rainfall mechanism: moisture can aid health while wetter conditions raise black-pod pressure; management is a confounder
records.reported_result: The wet south had the highest mean dry-bean yield and black-pod incidence; within-site weather variation did not significantly explain yield and management remained important
records.sample_or_data: 23 farms and 460 monitored cocoa trees from 2016 through 2019
records.title: Influences of climate variability on cocoa health and productivity in agroforestry systems in Ghana

records.authors: Esteban A. Montero-Sanchez; Danae M. A. Rozendaal; Ambra Tosto; Niels P. R. Anten; Pieter A. Zuidema
records.exposure: Monthly NASA POWER precipitation and temperature plus within-tree competition
records.external_validity_limits: Gridded monthly weather and observational associations; farm management disease and tree competition remain relevant; pod counts are not traded tonnes
records.lag: One to five months by pod class; black-pod association used a four-month climate lag
records.mechanism_use: Supports crop-stage lags and non-monotonic rainfall interpretation; does not establish a market signal
records.reported_result: Climate at fruit set best explained pod counts; higher temperature and precipitation reduced most pod classes and higher precipitation was associated with more black pod
records.sample_or_data: 1472 trees on 96 farms with pod counts about every six weeks
records.title: Effects of climate and within-tree competition on cocoa pod production in Ghana

records.authors: Salomon Obahoundje; Seifu A. Tilahun; Petra Schmitter
records.exposure: Drought excess-rainfall precipitation and temperature indices
records.external_validity_limits: Projection and model uncertainty; not a current crop forecast or causal estimate; regional yield outputs cannot be mapped directly into a trade
records.lag: Near future 2026-2055 and far future 2056-2085 relative to 1985-2014
records.mechanism_use: Supports regional rather than country-wide weather indicators and explicit drought/excess-rain cases
records.reported_result: Projected yield effects varied materially by region and scenario; severe drought cases were more damaging in vulnerable regions
records.sample_or_data: CHIRPS 1981-2024 plus 12 global climate models and regional yield modelling
records.study_type: Climate-model projection with machine-learning yield model
records.title: Climate-yield interactions in West Africa: Machine learning insights for cocoa production in Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire

translation_guardrails: Treat rainfall as non-monotonic: drought can damage cocoa, while excess rain and humidity can raise fungal-disease pressure.
Apply crop-stage and lag logic; Ghana pod observations found strongest climate associations at fruit set with one-to-five-month lags by pod class.
Do not transfer the magnitude of an extreme Bahia drought loss directly to Ghana or Cote d'Ivoire.
Do not convert a grid-cell weather anomaly to production tonnes without crop-area weights, phenology, farm management, disease, and validated yield response.
Observational and model-projection studies provide mechanism priors, not proof that a weather reading caused a market move or predicts returns.
